title: Bounding Box Collision
statement: Given two 2D rectangles (x, y, w, h), determine if they intersect or overlap. A standard game dev / industrial graphics problem.
hint: Check if one rectangle is completely to the left, right, top, or bottom of the other.

title: TCP State Transition
statement: Simulate a simplified TCP state machine. Given current state (LISTEN, SYN_RCVD, ESTABLISHED) and event (RCV_SYN, RCV_ACK), output the next state.
hint: Use a series of if/else to map (State, Event) to NewState.

title: Sensor Threshold Alarm
statement: An IoT temperature sensor reads a float. If Temp > 80, trigger HIGH_ALARM. If Temp < 0, trigger LOW_ALARM. If Temp between 70-80, trigger WARNING. Else NORMAL.
hint: Use if-else if-else chain.

title: Valid IPv4 Address
statement: Given four integers A, B, C, D representing an IP (A.B.C.D), verify if it is a valid IPv4 address (0-255 each) and not a loopback (127.x.x.x) or multicast (>=224.x.x.x).
hint: Check ranges for A, B, C, D and apply specific exclusions on A.

title: Bisection Root Finding Step
statement: In the bisection method, given bounds [a, b] and mid = (a+b)/2. If f(mid) == 0, return mid. If f(a)*f(mid) < 0, the root is in [a, mid], so update b = mid. Else a = mid.
hint: Use multiplication of function evaluations to determine sign changes.
output: Input: f(a)=-2, f(mid)=3 -> Output: New bounds [a, mid]

title: Two Sum (Sorted)
statement: Given a sorted array of integers and a target sum, find two numbers that add up to the target using a two-pointer approach.
hint: Initialize left = 0, right = n-1. Use a while(left < right) loop.

title: Binary Search
statement: Implement standard binary search on a sorted array. Return the index of the target or -1 if not found.
hint: Use while(low <= high) and calculate mid. Adjust low or high based on comparison.

title: Fast Inverse Square Root (Simulation)
statement: Simulate one iteration of Newton's method used in the Quake III Fast Inverse Square root algorithm to refine an initial guess for 1/sqrt(x).
output: Input: x=4, guess=0.5 -> Output: Refined guess

title: Greatest Common Divisor (Euclidean)
statement: Find the GCD of two numbers using the Euclidean algorithm.
hint: while(b != 0) { temp = b; b = a % b; a = temp; }

title: Linked List Cycle Detection (Floyd's)
statement: Simulate cycle detection using slow and fast pointers. The loop runs while fast and fast->next are not NULL.
hint: slow advances 1 step, fast advances 2 steps. If they meet, cycle exists.

title: Matrix Multiplication
statement: Multiply two matrices A (m x n) and B (n x p) to produce C (m x p).
hint: Requires 3 nested loops: i (rows of A), j (cols of B), k (inner dimension).

title: Bubble Sort Optimization
statement: Implement Bubble Sort but add a flag to break early if no swaps were made in the inner loop (early termination).
hint: Outer loop tracks passes, inner loop compares adjacents. Set swapped = false inside outer.

title: Image Convolution (3x3 Filter)
statement: Apply a 3x3 convolution matrix (like a Sobel edge detector) over a 2D array of pixels.
hint: Requires nested loops over the image pixels, and nested loops over the 3x3 kernel.
output: Input: 5x5 image, 3x3 kernel -> Output: 3x3 convolved image

title: Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Path
statement: Find the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in a weighted graph.
hint: Three nested loops: k (intermediate node), i (source node), j (destination node).
output: Input: Distance Matrix -> Output: Shortest Path Matrix

title: State Machine Parser
statement: Parse a simple command string (e.g., 'G', 'S', 'R') using a switch inside a loop to call respective functions (Go, Stop, Reverse).
hint: switch(char) { case 'G': ... case 'S': ... }

title: ALU Opcode Decoder
statement: Simulate an Arithmetic Logic Unit. Given an opcode (0=ADD, 1=SUB, 2=AND, 3=OR) and two operands, perform the operation.
hint: Switch on opcode to select the mathematical operation.

title: Hardware Interrupt Vector
statement: Simulate an embedded interrupt vector table. Switch on IRQ number (0-15) and dispatch to the correct simulated ISR.
hint: switch(irq) { case 0: handle_timer(); break; case 1: handle_gpio(); ... }
output: Input: IRQ=1 -> Output: GPIO ISR executed

title: Fibonacci Sequence
statement: Generate the first N numbers of the Fibonacci sequence.
hint: Use a for loop maintaining variables for the previous two numbers.

title: Array Reversal (In-Place)
statement: Reverse an array in-place without using a second array.
hint: Loop from i=0 to n/2, swap arr[i] with arr[n-1-i].

title: CRC-32 Checksum Simulation
statement: Simulate computing a simple CRC checksum over an array of bytes using a polynomial division (XOR) loop.
hint: For each bit in the byte, if MSB is 1, shift and XOR with polynomial.

title: Set, Clear, and Toggle Bit
statement: Write functions to set, clear, and toggle the nth bit of a given integer.
hint: Set: num | (1 << n). Clear: num & ~(1 << n). Toggle: num ^ (1 << n).
output: Input: num=5, bit=1 -> Output: Set=7, Clear=5, Toggle=7

title: Check if Power of Two
statement: Determine if a given positive integer is a power of 2 using only bitwise operators.
hint: Use (n & (n - 1)) == 0. A power of 2 has exactly one bit set.

title: Count Set Bits (Brian Kernighan's)
statement: Count the number of 1s in the binary representation of an integer in O(set bits) time.
hint: While n > 0, do n = n & (n - 1) and increment count.

title: Find Missing Number
statement: Given an array containing n distinct numbers taken from 0, 1, 2, ..., n, find the one that is missing using XOR.
hint: XOR all array elements and all numbers from 0 to n. The remaining value is the missing number.

title: Pointer to Array Elements
statement: Iterate over an array of integers using a pointer instead of array indexing (arr[i]).
hint: Initialize int *ptr = arr. Use *(ptr + i) to access elements.

title: Swap Two Numbers using Pointers
statement: Write a function swap(int *a, int *b) that swaps the values of the two variables.
hint: Dereference pointers to exchange values: int temp = *a; *a = *b; *b = temp;
output: Input: a=5, b=10 -> Output: a=10, b=5

title: Dynamic Memory Allocation
statement: Write a program that asks the user for array size N, allocates memory using malloc, populates it, and frees it.
hint: Use int *arr = (int *)malloc(N * sizeof(int)). Don't forget free(arr).
output: Input: N=3 -> Output: Memory allocated and freed.

title: Function Pointers Array
statement: Create an array of function pointers to represent a simple dispatch table (e.g., adding, subtracting).
hint: Declaration: int (*ops[])(int, int) = {add, sub}; Call: ops[0](5, 3);

title: Reverse Linked List
statement: Reverse a singly linked list iteratively by manipulating the next pointers.
hint: Maintain prev, curr, and next pointers. curr->next = prev.

title: Endianness Checker
statement: Write a C program to determine if the underlying architecture is Little Endian or Big Endian.
hint: Create an unsigned int i = 1. Cast its address to a char pointer and check the first byte.
output: Input: Run on x86 -> Output: Little Endian

title: Extract RGB from Hex (Bitmasking)
statement: Given a 24-bit color hex code (e.g., 0xFF5733), extract the Red, Green, and Blue components using bit shifts and masks.
hint: Red = (hex >> 16) & 0xFF. Green = (hex >> 8) & 0xFF. Blue = hex & 0xFF.

title: Check Substring
statement: Implement the strstr() function from scratch to find the first occurrence of a substring within a main string.
hint: Outer loop iterates through main string, inner loop checks characters of the substring.
output: Input: 'hello world', 'world' -> Output: Found at index 6

title: Kadane's Algorithm
statement: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum using a single pass O(n) algorithm.
hint: Keep track of max_so_far and current_max. If current_max drops below 0, reset it.

title: Duff's Device
statement: Implement Duff's device to manually unroll a loop for copying an array of bytes efficiently.
hint: Combine a switch statement and a while loop to jump into the middle of the loop block.
output: Input: Copy 20 bytes -> Output: Array copied with unrolled loop

title: State Machine with Switch
statement: Implement a vending machine state machine. States: IDLE, COIN_INSERTED, DISPENSE, RETURN_CHANGE.
hint: Use a switch(state) inside an infinite loop to handle state transitions.
output: Input: Insert Coin, Select Item -> Output: Dispense Item

title: Traffic Light
statement: Given R, Y, or G, print 'Stop', 'Wait', 'Go'.
hint: switch(char) { case 'R': ... }

title: Vowel Switch
statement: Check if char is vowel using fallthrough in switch.
hint: case 'a': case 'e': ... printf('Vowel');

title: Menu Driven DB
statement: Create a simple CRUD menu (1: Add, 2: Read, 3: Update, 4: Delete).
hint: switch(choice)

title: HTTP Status Codes
statement: Given status code (200, 404, 500), print the meaning.
hint: switch(code)

title: Sum of N
statement: Find sum of first N natural numbers using a loop.
hint: for(int i=1; i<=n; i++) sum += i;

title: Array Minimum
statement: Find the minimum element in an array.
hint: Initialize min = arr[0], loop through rest.

title: Linear Search
statement: Find index of an element in an array.
hint: Loop and check arr[i] == target.

title: Collatz Sequence
statement: Print Collatz sequence up to 10 iterations for a number.
hint: if even: n/2, if odd: 3n+1.

title: Count Digits
statement: Count number of digits in an integer.
hint: while(n!=0) { n/=10; count++; }

title: Palindrome Number
statement: Check if a number is palindrome.
hint: Reverse it using while loop, then compare with original.

title: Armstrong Number
statement: Check if a number is an Armstrong number.
hint: Sum of cubes of digits equals original number.

title: Number Pyramid
statement: Print a pyramid of numbers (1, 12, 123).
hint: Outer loop for rows, inner for numbers.

title: Pascal's Triangle
statement: Print first N rows of Pascal's triangle.
hint: Use binomial coefficient formula inside nested loops.

title: Matrix Transpose
statement: Transpose a 2D matrix.
hint: Swap arr[i][j] with arr[j][i].

title: Matrix Addition
statement: Add two matrices.
hint: res[i][j] = a[i][j] + b[i][j]

title: Find Duplicates
statement: Find duplicate elements in an array using two loops (O(N^2)).
hint: For i to n, For j=i+1 to n, if arr[i]==arr[j].

title: Odd or Even (Bitwise)
statement: Check if even or odd using bitwise AND.
hint: if (n & 1) odd else even.

title: Multiply by 2
statement: Multiply a number by 2 using bitwise shifts.

title: Divide by 2
statement: Divide a number by 2 using bitwise shifts.

title: Swap using XOR
statement: Swap two integers using XOR without a temp variable.
hint: a^=b; b^=a; a^=b;
output: Input: a=5, b=10 -> Output: a=10, b=5

title: String Length (Pointers)
statement: Find length of string using a pointer.
hint: while(*ptr != '�') ptr++;

title: Copy String
statement: Copy one string to another using pointers.
hint: while(*src) { *dest = *src; src++; dest++; }

title: Dynamic Array Realloc
statement: Allocate array of size N, then realloc to size 2N.
hint: arr = realloc(arr, 2*N*sizeof(int))

title: Pointer to Pointer
statement: Modify a pointer's address using a pointer to a pointer.
hint: void change(int **p) { *p = new_addr; }
output: Input: ptr -> Output: ptr points to new address
